inputs.root_cause: After exhausting the stale-duplicate-evidence sweep (event 225's suggestion, confirmed via systematic script that no more clean duplicate-cluster wins remained in xliff or any other format), surveyed xliff's remaining partial obligations for genuinely fresh, well-scoped capability. Found a 3-obligation cluster about the Metadata module's structural requirements (metaGroup required, meta requires type), entirely unbuilt: Metadata round-tripped only as opaque extension content with zero structural validation.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-234A057EBC798099 (XLIFF-PARSE-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-5450B2DB4BF7B672 (XLIFF-MODULE-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-72895F34A373C243 (XLIFF-MODEL-001) -- identical rule_text, all promoted partial->implemented
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 6 new tests prove validate() now detects Metadata module structural violations (missing metaGroup, meta missing type attribute at any nesting depth) while correctly leaving non-Metadata extensions untouched.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Confirmed via grep that no existing code inspects Metadata module structure at all -- modules.py only tracks namespace/coverage classification, and metadata round-trips as a generic ExtensionNode (raw bytes) via the reader's default extension fallback.

2. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 Metadata module XSD directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xlf-002.bin, schemas/metadata.xsd): mda:metadata's sequence declares minOccurs=1 maxOccurs=unbounded for mda:metaGroup children; mda:metaGroup is a choice of further metaGroup or meta (each minOccurs=1 maxOccurs=unbounded), confirming metaGroup nests recursively and meta can appear at any depth; mda:meta declares type use="required".

3. Added _metadata_module_diagnostics() to validator.py: scoped to only extensions whose tag matches the Metadata module's own qname, re-parses the extension's raw XML (same pattern as the existing _extension_well_formed check), flags a metadata element with no direct metaGroup child, and flags any meta element (found via ElementTree's recursive iter(), correctly handling any nesting depth) missing its type attribute.
4. Wired the new check alongside the existing _extension_well_formed() at all 3 call sites where extensions are walked: segment extensions, file/group-nested extensions, and root-level extensions.

5. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: a well-formed metadata tree validates cleanly; metadata with no metaGroup is a violation; a meta with no type is a violation; a meta nested inside a NESTED metaGroup (2 levels deep) is still correctly flagged missing type, proving the recursive walk; a non-Metadata-namespaced extension is untouched -- all 5 cases correct on the first attempt.

6. Checked existing test fixtures using Metadata module content (test_obligation_module_coverage.py) and confirmed they were already spec-conformant (meta already had a type attribute, metaGroup already present) -- no pre-existing-fixture fix needed this time, unlike the originalData tick.
7. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (409 tests, zero new fixtures) against the new check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 409 passed unchanged.
8. Wrote 6 formal tests, all passing on the first attempt.

9. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (415 passed, was 409, +6), and the full 6-format regression (3328 passed, was 3322, +6; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

10. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-a413ba4e6fac6da7, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/xliff/ -q -- 415 passed, was 409 passed (409 passed unchanged BEFORE writing new tests, confirming zero false positives)

.venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3328 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3322 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule; every claim grounded directly in the pinned XLIFF 2.1 Metadata module XSD.
